mode_marker.name: Mode Marker
mode_marker.description: One small marked work, one label, and the four ways the corpus says a label attaches to it - except that in the source it never attaches to the work at all. A 1.00 x 0.62 x 0.80 m deck carries a 0.66 m work and a 0.30 x 0.126 m paper mark, and `mode` walks the family's own vocabulary: float is the mark hanging in the air with no body, plate is the same mark on a card that has a front, stake is the same card on a post to the ground, decal is the mark alone again, printed on the work's own surface. Five registry names declare an axis called `mode` - gallery_marker_facade, gallery_marker_pattern, gallery_marker_soft-body and request_note all say float|plate|stake|decal, and synthesis_stand says auto|hero|series - but the four marker names are only TWO SCENES, because all three gallery_marker_* entries load the same file. Reading those two scripts corrects the ladder: `plate` sits on nothing in either member (gallery_marker's own comment says 'a bronze card standing on nothing'; request_note's plate keeps bobbing), and `decal` in both is a mark on the FLOOR, not on the work. There is no rung on which the marker touches the thing it marks, because in the source there is no thing it marks. This bench supplies the missing referent and then tests it: `subject` builds three works read off the family's own roster - a facade with bare ground at its foot, a wallpaper field that covers the ground edge to edge because a plane group has no outside, and a settled cushion with a domed top. On the field, a post that must MEET THE FLOOR has no floor to meet, so `stake` falls back to `plate` and the two modes are one photograph. Nothing animates, nothing is random, nothing bakes on a worker thread.
dev_themes: one scene wearing three registry names
a fallback that is an identity
interactions: walk `mode` on the facade subject and watch the marker acquire things: float is the mark alone in the air, plate puts a body behind it, stake puts a foot under the body, decal takes the body away again and puts the mark on the wall. Three of the four are placed by the room; only the last is placed by the work

put plate and stake side by side on `pattern` and look for the post. It is not there and nothing is broken - the field covers the deck edge to edge, so a post that must meet the floor has no floor to meet. Those two tiles are the same photograph, and that is the argument
put the same pair side by side on `facade` and on `soft_body`: the post is back, standing on bare deck in both, because a facade and a cushion leave ground around them and a wallpaper group does not

walk `subject` at mode=decal and watch one rule produce three marks: flat on the facade's face, stepped by up to 0.17 m across its own 0.30 m width on the relief field, and domed on the cushion's crown. The sheet samples the work's surface function; the work decides what the sheet does

walk `subject` at mode=float and notice that nothing about the marker changes at all. The mark is at the same three coordinates in every subject, because a marker that has committed to nothing has nothing to be changed by
mode_marker.capacity: SEE that the family's four-word vocabulary is a ladder of commitment to a PLACE, not to a work - and that the top rung, the one whose name promises a mark printed on the thing itself, is implemented in both members as a mark on the floor

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The STAGE is the footprint and it is drawn before either axis is consulted: a 1.00 x 0.80 m deck and a 0.026 m datum mast at the back-left corner topping out at 0.62 m. The three works run 0.66 x 0.528 x 0.15 (facade), 1.00 x 0.220 x 0.80 (pattern, which covers the whole deck by construction) and 0.66 x 0.420 x 0.33 (soft_body), and the marker's own reach runs from y 0.024 at the stake's foot to y 0.485 at the plate's emissive edge - so the FIGURE changes shape completely across the sheet while the world box stays 1.00 x 0.62 x 0.80 in all twelve cells. That is why the mast exists. Nothing is yawed to face the camera. layout=ladder stands all four modes in a row at 1.30 m pitch, about 5.0 m wide, and is a design view rather than a map placement.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry against the constants in mode_marker.gd; no Godot was run. The box is the STAGE and nothing else: the deck spans x +-0.50 and z +-0.40, and the datum mast at (-0.455, -0.355) tops out at 0.62 m, which is above the tallest thing any cell draws (the facade's cornice at 0.552). The works themselves measure 0.66 x 0.528 x 0.15, 1.00 x 0.220 x 0.80 and 0.66 x 0.420 x 0.33, which is exactly why the mast is there: without it the union AABB would be set by whichever cell held the facade and the pattern cells would be photographed as a different experiment.

dna.default: mode=float, subject=facade. THE COUNT IS NOT UNANIMOUS AND THE TIEBREAK IS SAID OUT LOUD. By registry name it is 3 to 1 for `stake`: gallery_marker_pattern and gallery_marker_soft-body both carry "default": "mode=stake - the shipped code path", gallery_marker_facade carries no default key at all (and lists its values in a different order, stake first), and request_note carries "default": "mode=float - the pre-promotion behaviour, so all 716 existing placements are unchanged". By SCENE it is 1 to 1, because the three stake votes are gallery_marker.gd counted three times - `@export_enum(...) var mode: String = "stake"` is one line in one file. The tie is broken by placements, counted in commons/maps: request_note 724, gallery_marker_facade 22, gallery_marker_pattern 10, gallery_marker_soft-body 24, so 724 against 56, 12.9 to 1 for float. `float` is also the ladder's zero rung - the marker that has committed to nothing - which makes it the honest reference the other three are measured against. subject=facade because it is the only one of the three on which all four attachments are constructible, so the default cell is the case with no fallback in it.
dna.note:
WHAT THE VALUES MEAN, where each word came from, and which of them the code does not honour.

THE FAMILY FIRST, as a census. FIVE registry names declare an axis called `mode`, and a sixth declares the word in a completely different sense. gallery_marker_facade, gallery_marker_pattern, gallery_marker_soft-body and request_note all declare float | plate | stake | decal. synthesis_stand declares auto | hero | series. SphericalHarmonics declares l1_m0 | l2_m0 | l2_m1 | l3_m2 | l4_m4 | l5_m2 - spherical-harmonic (l, m) indices, a mode in the physics sense - and is named as kin and excluded.

FOUR NAMES, TWO SCENES. All three gallery_marker_* entries name res://commons/artifacts/gallery_marker/gallery_marker.tscn. One script, one geometry, three lookup names separated by a label string, and the registry entry says so itself: "only the label FACADE, injected through apply_grid_config, distinguishes it from its PATTERN and other siblings. You-are-here turns out to be a config string, not a geometry." This is the corpus's most common hidden family in its plainest form, and it matters twice: it halves the default vote (see `default`), and it means the four-word vocabulary has two authors, not four, so agreement between them is worth less than it looks.

DO THE TWO AUTHORS AGREE ABOUT THE FOUR WORDS? Yes, and gallery_marker says so in its own header: "`mode` is REUSED VERBATIM from request_note - same word, same level of the grammar, same meaning, same four values in the same order... So this is one artifact joining an existing family, not founding a synonym." That is a rare thing in this corpus and it is the reason the vocabulary is worth a bench.

THE THING THE CODE SAYS THAT THE BRIEF DID NOT, and it is the finding. The brief read the four words as a ladder of how much a marker COMMITS TO THE THING IT MARKS: float hovers touching nothing, plate sits on a surface, stake is driven into the ground beside it, decal is printed ON the object and cannot be removed without damaging the work. TWO OF THOSE FOUR ARE NOT WHAT EITHER MEMBER BUILDS.

  `plate` DOES NOT SIT ON ANYTHING. gallery_marker._build_plate() builds a card whose own comment reads "a bronze card standing on nothing, lower edge at 0.95 m". request_note's plate branch is _build_card(Vector3(0, hover_height, 0), false) - grounded FALSE - and because grounded is false the _bobs flag is never cleared, so the plate is still hovering AND still riding request_note's sine bob in _process. The only thing plate adds over float, in both members, is that the text is printed ON something and stops billboarding: it acquires a body and a front, not a footing.

  `decal` IS ON THE FLOOR, NOT ON THE WORK. gallery_marker._build_decal() is a 0.62 m roundel with an emissive inlay ring, laid flat, and its comment is "You do not look AT this marker, you stand on it." request_note._build_decal() is a card at y = 0.006 with its label rotated -90 about X. Neither is printed on anything except the ground.

SO THERE IS NO RUNG ON WHICH THE MARKER TOUCHES WHAT IT MARKS, and the reason is structural rather than an oversight: IN BOTH MEMBERS THERE IS NO THING BEING MARKED. The marker is the whole artifact; the only other body in the scene is the floor. The ladder that is actually implemented runs nothing -> a body -> a foot on the floor -> the floor itself, and it is a ladder of commitment to a PLACE. That is a weaker and more interesting claim than the brief's, and it is checkable in two files.

MODE, four values, the family's order.

  float - BOTH MEMBERS, and it is request_note's default. gallery_marker._build_float() is a one-line function: _build_label(), a billboarded Label3D at 1.16 m and nothing else. request_note._build_float() is a Label3D at hover_height with a sine bob, and its header calls it "the most-placed artifact in the project - 716 placements... naked floating text, which is the one thing the cabinet grammar's first rule forbids". Here: the 0.30 x 0.126 m paper mark alone, 0.004 m thick, at (0.0, 0.40, 0.312), with 0.313 m of air below it. NO BODY, NO FRONT, NO CONTACT. THE ONE THING DECLINED IS THE BILLBOARD (see `declines`), because a billboard is a fact about the camera and would make the axis unmeasurable from a second standpoint.

  plate - BOTH MEMBERS, AND THEY DISAGREE ABOUT WHAT THE CARD IS MADE OF. gallery_marker's is BRONZE - marker_color.darkened(0.25), roughness 0.5, metallic 0.55 - with a thin emissive band along the top edge, kept there "so the plate reads as the same object in another body, not a different artifact". request_note's card IS the paper: PAPER (0.90, 0.87, 0.80) with a 0.030 m tone stripe down the leading edge, and the text is printed on it. This bench takes BOTH, because they are answering different halves: request_note's paper-and-stripe is THE MARK, identical in all four modes, and gallery_marker's bronze card with its emissive edge is THE CARRIER that `plate` adds behind it. The mark's plane is at the same world z in float and in plate, so plate adds a body and moves nothing.

  stake - BOTH MEMBERS, AND THEY SAY THE SAME SENTENCE. gallery_marker.gd: "a mark on a post that MEETS THE FLOOR (the shipped build, default)". request_note.gd: "A surveyor's stake. The note MEETS THE FLOOR - for a todo about a place rather than about the air above it." The floor, in both, in capitals in one of them. Here: the plate's card unchanged, plus a 12-gon post of radius 0.018 running from the deck to the card's lower edge, plus request_note's painted band at the foot (0.06 m tall, 1.167x the post radius, verbatim). The post's proportion is gallery_marker's - 10.2 percent of the card's width against its own 11 percent - not request_note's 3.9 percent, which on a 0.352 m card would be 7 mm and invisible to a still.

  decal - BOTH MEMBERS, AND THIS IS WHERE THE BENCH DEVIATES ON PURPOSE. Both build a mark on the ground. This bench builds the word instead: the mark alone again, no carrier, its sample points read off the WORK'S OWN SURFACE FUNCTION. One rule, three outcomes - flat on the facade's face, stepped on the relief field, domed on the cushion's crown. It is the only mode whose position the work dictates; float, plate and stake are all at (0.0, *, 0.30), the room's coordinates, in every subject. THE DEVIATION IS DECLARED RATHER THAN SMUGGLED (see `declines`), because it is the single change that makes this axis about the work at all, and a reader is entitled to say the bench built the ladder it wanted.

SUBJECT, three values, and it is THIS SYNTHESIS'S OWN AXIS in the sense that no member declares it - but not in the sense that it was invented, because three of the four marker names ARE the names of what they mark. gallery_marker_facade anchors the facades sequence; gallery_marker_pattern anchors Pattern_pt01..pt10, the wallpaper groups; gallery_marker_soft-body anchors softbodies. The axis asks what those three things are, geometrically, and whether an attachment is available on each.

  facade - a FRONT: plinth, wall, cornice and four pilasters, 0.66 x 0.528 x 0.15, standing on bare deck. One flat vertical face at z = 0.045, and floor all round its foot. ALL FOUR ATTACHMENTS ARE AVAILABLE, which is why it is the default and the reference. The pilasters are pushed out to x +-0.190 and +-0.265 so the middle 0.32 m of the face is clear: that clearance is where the decal goes, and a pilaster proud of the face would put 20 mm of stone in front of it.

  pattern - a FIELD, 11 x 9 relief cells covering the WHOLE deck, 1.00 x 0.80, four heights on an integer motif (a checker, with the (0,0) cell of every 4 x 4 block at the top step and (2,2) at the third). Edge to edge is not a stylistic choice: a plane group is infinite by construction and has no outside, and the maps it anchors are mosaic floors. So THERE IS NO GROUND BESIDE THE WORK. A post that must meet the floor has no floor to meet, and `stake` falls back to what it can still build - the card in the air, which is `plate`. And there is no single surface either: the field's top is at four heights, so the decal STEPS, by up to 0.17 m inside its own 0.30 m width.

  soft_body - a settled CUSHION: a 0.20 m base slab under a dome of up to 0.22 m, flanks barrelling 10 percent outward at mid-height and back to nominal at both ends, 0.66 x 0.420 x 0.33. Bare deck all around it, so the stake stands. But its surface is curved, so the decal follows it (the sheet drops 0.049 m from crown to corner across its own width) and the plate, hanging in the room at a fixed height, does not - which is the difference the word `soft` is supposed to name and which no member's `mode` has ever had anything to be soft against.

THE INTERACTION IS THE CLAIM. mode x subject is not two independent knobs: the subject decides which rungs of the ladder exist. On facade all four are distinct. On soft_body all four are distinct and two of them (plate, decal) disagree about the surface. On pattern the ladder LOSES A RUNG, and the loss is silent in the frame - two tiles, one photograph - which is why it is pre-registered below rather than discovered afterwards.

THE EXTENTS, because a stake reaches down and a float reaches up. The marker's own band across all four modes runs y 0.024 (the stake's foot on the deck) to y 0.485 (the plate's top edge, where the emissive band sits), 0.461 m. The works run to y 0.552 (facade), 0.244 (pattern) and 0.444 (soft_body). The datum mast tops out at 0.62 m, above all of them, so the union AABB is 1.00 x 0.62 x 0.80 with centre (0, 0.31, 0) in every one of the twelve cells and the camera never moves. At framing 0.62 the subject fills about 72 percent of the frame's width and 55 percent of its height.

THE DRAWN AREA OF THE MARK, because a marker is small and the critic has a blank floor at about 0.2 percent of frame. The paper face is 0.30 x 0.126 = 0.0378 m2, which is 14.7 percent of the facade's own front face (0.258 m2). At the sweep's standpoint it projects to 0.0297 m2 upright (cos 0.7865) and 0.0097 m2 laid flat (cos 0.2571) - 2.66 and 0.87 percent of the subject crop, 1.06 and 0.35 percent of the frame. The flat case is the smallest thing in this sheet and it is the one that had to be checked, because the decal on pattern and on soft_body is horizontal.

HOW THE SHEET IS PROTECTED FROM THE COLOUR TRAP. The critic measures luminance and has a separate per-channel rescue, so a pair separated only by hue at constant brightness reads as a twin. NO PAIR HERE IS SEPARATED BY HUE ALONE: float against plate adds a card silhouette, plate against stake adds a post silhouette, decal moves the mark onto another surface at another angle, and every subject pair is a different body. If the colour-only rescue fires on this sheet it is reporting a fault, not a rescue.

THE THESIS SOMEONE COULD DISAGREE WITH: the family's four words are not a ladder of commitment to the thing marked - they are a ladder of commitment to a PLACE, and the top rung's name promises the first while the code delivers the second. The proof offered is that three of the four modes are placed by the room in every subject, and the fourth had to be REBUILT to be placed by the work at all. THE DISAGREEMENT AVAILABLE, and it is fair: a reader can say the bench invented the referent, built `decal` the way it wanted, and then proved the source lacks it. The answer is that the WORD is the source's, that both members' decal is on the floor and can be read in ten lines each, and that a vocabulary is a claim about what can be said. The cell where holding the thesis costs something is stake on pattern, where a bench that thinks a stake needs a floor is obliged to publish two identical tiles and call it a finding.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: plate against stake, on the facade subject
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic:
Computed BEFORE ANY CAPTURE in the critic's own currency, by projecting the constants in mode_marker.gd through capture_config_sweep's camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, framing 0.62 on the union AABB of all twelve variants, which is the STAGE at 1.00 x 0.62 x 0.80 and therefore identical in every cell) and through artifact_dna_critic's pipeline: crop to the subject box, neutralise each frame's own corner, grey, resize 160 x 160, mean of the hottest 5 percent.

THE CONTEXT IS THE `facade` SUBJECT AND THE RANKING IS COMPUTED INSIDE IT. Six pairs, focus percent: plate-stake 6.7, float-plate 11.7, float-stake about 19, float-decal about 26, plate-decal about 30, stake-decal about 35. Naming the pair without naming the subject would be meaningless here, because on `pattern` this same pair is 0.00 by construction.

WHY THAT PAIR. plate and stake share the card, the emissive edge, the mark, the stripe and their world positions to the vertex; the ENTIRE difference in the frame is one post and its foot band. Camera basis at yaw 0.62 / pitch -0.26: view direction (0.5615, 0.2571, 0.7865), screen right (0.8138, 0, -0.5810), screen up (-0.1494, 0.9663, -0.2092). The post is a 12-gon of radius 0.018 running y 0.024 to 0.315 at (0, *, 0.30), so it projects 0.036 m wide by 0.2812 m tall; the foot band is radius 0.021, 0.060 tall at y 0.100. Total changed area 0.01057 m2, times 1.113 for perspective at that depth = 0.01177 m2, against a subject crop of 1.2054 x 0.9257 = 1.1158 m2 - so 1.055 percent of the compared pixels, 270 of 25600, against a hottest-5-percent window of 1280. THE WINDOW DOES NOT FILL, so the number is set by area as well as contrast and the dilution is 270/1280 = 0.211.

THE CONTRAST IS NOT ONE NUMBER, which is why the facade has three stones. Going up the post: 0.043 of its screen height stands against the deck (Rec.709 grey 0.200 against the post's 0.304, delta 0.104), 0.084 against the plinth and its top face (0.582, delta 0.278), 0.148 against the wall (0.721, delta 0.417); the accent band (0.648) covers 0.053 of that height and reads 0.448 against the deck and 0.066 against the plinth. Area-weighted mean delta 0.316, so focus = 270 x 0.316 / 1280 = 6.7 percent.

6.7 IS BARELY OVER THE CRITIC'S TWIN BAR OF 6.0, AND THAT IS SAID IN ADVANCE. If the render adds nothing this pair will be reported as a TWIN, and that report would be correct rather than a fault: a stake is a plate that has grown a foot, and the foot is one percent of the picture. THE PREDICTION IS A FLOOR, NOT A FORECAST - this arithmetic has one light, flat shading, no shadow, no AO and no antialiasing, and a post standing on a deck is exactly the geometry a contact shadow doubles, so 10 to 20 percent is the expected landing and every prior prediction in this corpus under-read by 1.5x to 6.7x.

IF THE SWEEP COMES BACK BELOW 6.7 ON THE NAMED PAIR, STOP AND INVESTIGATE THE HARNESS BEFORE THE DESIGN: (a) tools/check_dna_declarations.py - a value the code cannot reach falls back to the default and prints identical tiles; (b) _rejects.json - all three exports are String enums and Object.set() on a typed property of the wrong type is refused in SILENCE; (c) whether the sheet was captured with --max=12, because at build_dna_gallery's default cap of 9 the 4 x 3 cross product is trimmed from the tail of the LATER axis and `subject` collapses, which deletes the designed null and with it the whole interaction.

THE PAIR AT REAL RISK IS ELSEWHERE AND IS NOT THE REGISTERED NUMBER. plate against decal on `soft_body` depends on the dome being legible in shading rather than in silhouette: the decal drops only 0.049 m from crown to corner across its own 0.30 m, and if the rig's key light is flat enough that curve could read as a plane. That would not make the axis inert - the mark still moves from the air to the cushion - but it would make the soft_body subject argue less than it claims.

designed_nulls.why: IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION AND IT IS THE THESIS, not a spare check. Both members define `stake` in the same words - a mark on a post that MEETS THE FLOOR (gallery_marker.gd:34) and "The note MEETS THE FLOOR" (request_note.gd:136). On `pattern` the field covers the deck edge to edge, because a plane group has no outside, so there is no floor for a post to meet; the bench builds what remains buildable, which is the card in the air, which IS `plate`. The two cells therefore emit the same four meshes in the same order with the same vertices: Card, CardEdge, Mark, MarkStripe. Predicted 0.00 percent focus / 0.00 percent frame; anything above 0.5 percent is render noise, and anything above 2 percent means the post is being built somewhere it cannot stand. THE SAME PAIR IS 6.7 PERCENT ON `facade` AND ABOUT THE SAME ON `soft_body`, which is what makes this a fact about the subject rather than about the axis - and it is the reason `subject` is not a decoration around `mode` but the thing that decides how many rungs `mode` has.

dna.designed_nulls_why: ONE NULL, AND ONLY ONE, BECAUSE ONLY ONE CELL LOSES AN ATTACHMENT. Every other combination of the two axes is constructible and distinct: on `facade` and on `soft_body` all four modes build different geometry, and on `pattern` the other three do too - float and plate hang above the field, decal steps across it. No fallback was invented to manufacture a second null. THE TEMPTING FALSE ONE is decal on `pattern` against decal on `soft_body`, where both marks are horizontal sheets of the same 0.30 x 0.126 m paper at the same plan position: they are NOT a null, because one steps by up to 0.17 m and the other domes by 0.049 m, and the works under them share no vertex. If that pair comes back under 2 percent the finding is that the critic cannot see a 49 mm dome at this framing, which is a fact about the instrument and is written into `predicted_degeneracy` as the pair at risk. If the one registered null comes back above 2 percent, nothing else in this sheet can be believed.
dna.fixture_why: The bench can stand all four modes in a row (layout=ladder, 1.30 m pitch, about 5.0 m wide) but the SWEEP must see one at a time: capture_config_sweep unions the AABB across a spec's variants, so a four-wide row in the same spec would frame every single cell against five metres and photograph the post as a hair. layout is an export and not an axis, and it ships at single, so the fixture is a belt over braces. WHAT IS NOT FIXTURED, AND WHY NOTHING NEEDS TO BE: there is no clock and no random number here. The whole figure is built synchronously inside _ready from arithmetic on declared constants - no _process, no Timer, no randf, no FastNoiseLite, and deliberately no NoiseTexture2D, which bakes on a worker thread and would let the shutter catch an unbaked map. That matters because one source is not so quiet: request_note runs a _process that bobs the whole node by sin(t * 1.5) * 0.015 in TWO of its four modes (float and plate, the ones where _bobs is never cleared), so a sweep of request_note itself photographs two of its values at an unknown phase and two at rest. This bench does not bob, and that is recorded in `declines`.
dna.kin:
SphericalHarmonics IS KIN AND IS EXCLUDED, and the reason is the plainest kind: it is a different word. Its `mode` is l1_m0 | l2_m0 | l2_m1 | l3_m2 | l4_m4 | l5_m2 - spherical-harmonic (l, m) index pairs, mode in the physics sense of a standing-wave solution, and its own registry note says what the axis asks: "WHICH one, over real (l, m) pairs - the dipole, two readings of degree 2 that separate l from m, a sectoral l=m, and a fine high-degree band." There is no rung, no attachment and no marker anywhere in it. Sweeping it beside float|plate|stake|decal would be sweeping a homonym, and the resulting sheet would be six pictures of a sphere next to four pictures of a sign, with a shared column heading and nothing else shared. Named here rather than silently dropped because the collision is exactly the thing a `mode` census is for.

SYNTHESIS_STAND IS THE OTHER EXCLUSION AND IT IS A SUBTLER ONE, WORTH SAYING BECAUSE IT IS THE CORPUS'S OWN FURNITURE FOR DISPLAYING WHAT THIS PROGRAMME MAKES. Its `mode` is auto | hero | series, and its truth line is "a default is merely the branch that got walked. The hero is the branch the numbers argue for; the series is the family refusing to pick." That is a question about how a STAND PRESENTS ITS OCCUPANT - one pinned variant on a slab, or the whole family on a rail in measured order of departure - not about how a label attaches to a work. Same word, adjacent grammar, different level. AND `auto` IS A DISPATCH VALUE, WHICH IS THE ALL-RUNGS FAULT IN ITS PUREST FORM: synthesis_stand.gd:79-83 reads commons/data/dna_synthesis.json and then sets form to "hero" or "series" (and to "hero" again when the verdict is "default" or "unmeasured"). A sweep of [auto, hero, series] therefore photographs one of the other two values TWICE, under a third name, with the duplicate chosen by a data file rather than by the axis - and which one it duplicates changes when the file changes. It is 39 placements, so this is not a hypothetical.

THE FOUR MARKER NAMES ARE THE REAL KIN, and the relation is unusually direct because this bench shares their word rather than inventing one. request_note is the project's own annotation apparatus and the most-placed artifact in it - 724 placements counted in commons/maps - and its truth is that a todo lives at the coordinates it complains about. gallery_marker is a you-are-here anchor whose registry entry confesses that its siblings differ by a config string. A room holding this bench beside request_note is saying the same sentence twice about a note; a room holding it beside gallery_marker_facade is saying the sentence and then showing the wall the sign has never been allowed to touch.
declines: THE BRIEF'S LADDER, CORRECTED FROM THE CODE, and it is the biggest change. The brief said the axis runs from a caption that could be about anything to a mark that cannot be removed without damaging the work, with `plate` sitting on a surface and `decal` printed on the object. TWO OF THE FOUR RUNGS ARE NOT BUILT THAT WAY. gallery_marker's plate is "a bronze card standing on nothing" in its own comment; request_note's plate passes grounded=false and keeps bobbing. gallery_marker's decal is a roundel on the GROUND ("you do not look AT this marker, you stand on it") and request_note's is a card at y = 0.006 on the GROUND. So the implemented ladder is nothing -> a body -> a foot on the floor -> the floor itself: commitment to a PLACE, not to a work. The bench is built the same way either reading; the note now says which is true.

THE BILLBOARD, and it is the deviation that protects the measurement. `float` billboards in both members (gallery_marker sets BILLBOARD_ENABLED, request_note sets BILLBOARD_ENABLED) and plate, stake and decal all disable it - so in the source, orientation is part of what the axis changes. A billboarded mark is a fact about where the camera is standing, and this corpus has already convicted five of seven dead verdicts of being facts about one standpoint. Building it would make `float` unmeasurable from any second standpoint and would make the anamorphic probe meaningless on this token. The mark here faces +Z in every mode. What is lost is real and is named: in the source, float is the only mode with no orientation of its own, and this sheet cannot show that.

`decal` ON THE FLOOR, which is what both members actually build, in favour of `decal` on the work. This is the change that makes the axis about the work at all, and it is the one a reader is most entitled to challenge. The defence is that the word means printed-on and both members' comments describe the ground rather than the work because there is no work in either scene to print on; the accusation available is that the bench built the ladder it wanted and then found the source lacking. Both are written down. What is NOT invented is the fallback: when a mode's attachment is unavailable the bench builds what remains, and it does that in exactly one cell.

THE BOB. request_note._process moves the whole node by sin(_time * 1.5) * 0.015 whenever _bobs is true, which is float and plate but not stake or decal - so two of its four values are photographed at an unknown phase and two at rest, and a 15 mm vertical offset on a 0.62 m card is about 2.4 percent of its height. A sweep of request_note's own `mode` has therefore always been comparing two moving tiles against two still ones. Not built here, and flagged rather than fixed, because fixing it would change the look of 724 placements.

THE LABEL. Every member's mark is a Label3D carrying text - FACADE, PATTERN, SOFT BODY, or a request string loaded from a map's requests.json. Text is declined here for two reasons and only two: a Label3D's rendered width depends on a font resource that is not part of this file, so two builds of one value would not be guaranteed identical; and the axis is about the mark's BODY, which is the one thing the members' own headers insist the word names ("it names the BODY of a text-carrying MARKER and nothing else in this vocabulary may spend it on anything else"). The paper-and-stripe shape is request_note's card verbatim in proportion; only the glyphs are missing.

`tone` FROM request_note (request | bug | question | done) AS A THIRD AXIS. It is the member's OTHER question - the register the note speaks in, driving an accent colour and a corner glyph - and it is orthogonal to attachment: a bug can be a stake or a decal. A bench that swept it beside `mode` would be answering two questions in one sheet and could not attribute either. Its accent colour IS used here, at the `request` value, so the stripe and the foot band are the family's own orange rather than a new one.

A FIFTH SUBJECT, and specifically a subject with no surface at all - a light, a sound, a rule. That is where the ladder would break hardest, since three of the four modes would fall back and the null would be a triple rather than a pair. Declined because there is no member to derive it from: all three subjects here are read off marker names that exist, and inventing a fourth would be inventing the answer.

THE ROUNDEL. gallery_marker's decal is a 0.62 m disc with an emissive inlay ring and a fill disc, and it is a nice object. It is declined because it is a floor form: a disc laid on a facade's vertical face reads as a porthole, and a disc that changed shape per subject would confound the decal cells with a form change. The mark keeps one rectangle in all four modes so that only its placement can differ.

A LARGER MARK. At 0.30 x 0.126 m the paper is 14.7 percent of the facade's front face, and every pair in the sheet would read hotter if it were bigger. It is not, because the family's own headers call this thing wayfinding furniture that is "never dominant", and because the closest pair predicted here is about a post rather than about the mark - inflating the mark would raise the floor under every number without making the predicted pair any easier to see.

GODOT 3 NAMING, NOT PRESENT BUT CHECKED FOR. Neither member carries a flags_* property, so the stale-API fault that bites about twenty files in this corpus does not apply to this family. Recorded because the absence was verified rather than assumed.
dna.sweep_note: THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=12 AND THE COST OF GETTING IT WRONG IS THE INTERACTION. `mode` is declared first and is never trimmed; `subject` is second, and build_dna_gallery trims the LATER axis from the tail until the cross product fits its cap. At the default --max=9 the 4 x 3 sheet renders as 4 x 2 = facade and pattern only, which keeps the designed null but deletes soft_body and therefore the whole surface-following half of the decal argument; worse, a cap of 8 or below would leave `facade` alone, which is the one subject on which nothing falls back and the sheet would show a clean four-rung ladder with no claim in it at all. Only 12 carries the experiment.
